Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates LLM-based software engineering agents on real GitHub issues where the model must generate a code patch that makes the project’s tests pass. The “Verified” subset contains tasks validated by human engineers to be solvable and is commonly reported as pass@1 under a fixed agent scaffold.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style bug-fixing to multiple programming languages and ecosystems, requiring models to adapt their coding behaviors beyond Python-centric tooling. Tasks still involve repository understanding, patch generation, and test-based validation, but across varied syntax, libraries, and build systems.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a larger and more difficult software engineering benchmark intended to be more contamination-resistant and more reflective of professional, multi-language development work. Models must implement correct patches in real repositories under evaluation harness constraints, typically reported as pass@1.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Self-reflection (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 measures agentic performance on real command-line tasks executed in sandboxed environments (e.g., debugging, installing dependencies, manipulating files, running programs). Success depends on iteratively using tool feedback (stdout/stderr, exit codes) to converge on a correct terminal workflow under step and resource limits.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: BrowseComp evaluates “deep research” abilities where models must search and synthesize information from a controlled document corpus or web-like index to answer challenging questions. It stresses retrieval strategy, evidence tracking, and producing a final justified answer in a single attempt or constrained agent setting.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: τ2-bench measures how well an agent conducts multi-turn task completion with a simulated user while interacting with domain APIs (e.g., retail, airline, telecom) and adhering to policies. It emphasizes robust tool use, policy-following under pressure, and conversational coordination over long interaction trajectories.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control

Description: OSWorld benchmarks multimodal “computer use” where an agent must complete tasks by operating within an operating-system-like GUI using screenshots and actions (click, type, navigate). It probes perception-to-action grounding, interface understanding, and step-by-step planning under a bounded action budget.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Working Memory, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a “fluid reasoning” benchmark of abstract grid transformations where each task provides a few input-output examples and requires inferring the rule to transform a novel input. It is designed to emphasize generalization and rule induction rather than memorized domain knowledge.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence by simulating management of a vending-machine business over an extended period, with performance scored by final financial outcome. Agents must plan, negotiate, track inventory, adapt pricing, and maintain consistency across many sequential decisions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas tests real-world tool use through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), requiring models to discover tools, call them correctly, handle errors, and compose multi-step workflows across servers. It reflects production-like API orchestration and robustness in tool-driven task execution.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates tasks characteristic of entry-level financial analysis, such as interpreting financial documents, performing calculations, building models, and producing analyst-style outputs. It stresses domain knowledge application, structured reasoning, and multi-step artifact generation rather than single fact recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agent capabilities on large suites of tasks including identifying known vulnerabilities from descriptions and, in some settings, discovering new vulnerabilities in real open-source projects. Performance depends on code comprehension, hypothesis generation about exploits, and iterative debugging/testing in constrained environments.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench assesses an agent’s ability to navigate, edit, and compute with complex spreadsheets derived from real-world scenarios. Tasks require locating relevant cells/sheets, applying correct formulas or transformations, and producing correctly formatted outputs under tool-based execution.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Working Memory, Decision-making, Attention, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3:

Description: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) is a broad, frontier-level benchmark spanning difficult questions across many domains and modalities, often requiring multi-step reasoning and, in some settings, tool use (search/code). It is intended to approximate the outer edge of expert knowledge work rather than narrow academic quizzes.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Planning (minor)
L3:

Description: AIME 2025 evaluates competition-style mathematics problems from the American Invitational Mathematics Examination, typically requiring multi-step symbolic reasoning and careful constraint handling. Scores are reported as accuracy over the problem set, sometimes with or without tool assistance.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: GPQA Diamond is a curated subset of the GPQA benchmark consisting of very difficult graduate-level multiple-choice science questions designed to be “Google-proof.” It emphasizes deep scientific reasoning and discrimination among close distractors rather than surface-level recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU into multiple languages, testing broad academic knowledge and reasoning across many subjects with multilingual prompts. It probes whether a model’s competence generalizes beyond English and across language-specific phrasing and conventions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark spanning many disciplines where answering requires integrating text with images (e.g., diagrams, charts, figures) to solve problems. It evaluates multimodal grounding and reasoning, often under multiple-choice formats.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU-Pro is an updated, more challenging variant of MMMU designed to better measure expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning. It typically increases difficulty via harder questions, stronger distractors, and/or more demanding visual interpretation requirements.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Attention, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA evaluates whether models can correctly interpret scientific figures from biology papers and answer questions grounded in those figures. It stresses accurate visual reading (plots, panels, annotations) and scientific context integration rather than general image captioning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Attention, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3:

Description: WebArena benchmarks autonomous web agents performing realistic tasks across multiple web apps (e-commerce, forums, GitLab-like tools, CMS) using a browser interface. Success depends on navigating dynamic pages, filling forms correctly, and planning multi-step workflows end-to-end.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MathArena Apex is a competition-style math benchmark collection intended to be difficult and discriminative at the frontier, often aggregating harder problem sets and reporting accuracy and/or rating-based metrics. It emphasizes multi-step mathematical reasoning, careful bookkeeping, and solution robustness under time/attempt constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates models on understanding and reasoning over high-resolution screenshots of software interfaces from professional contexts. Tasks often require identifying UI elements, interpreting layout, and extracting correct answers grounded in visual interface details.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: CharXiv Reasoning tests scientific figure and chart understanding by asking questions grounded in figures from research papers, often requiring quantitative interpretation. It rewards precise extraction of visual evidence, mapping figure semantics to text, and multi-step reasoning (sometimes with code tools).
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: OmniDocBench 1.5 evaluates document understanding and OCR-like capabilities across heterogeneous elements such as text blocks, formulas, tables, and reading order. It measures whether models can faithfully recover structured content and layout-sensitive information from document images.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception, Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Attention, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: Video-MMMU extends multimodal understanding to the video setting, requiring models to answer questions that depend on temporal visual information across frames. It stresses integrating events over time, tracking salient details, and combining visual cues with language prompts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Attention, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Timing & Predictive Modeling (minor)

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates coding performance on timed/competitive programming-style tasks with strong anti-contamination intent, often summarized via an ELO-like rating. It measures algorithmic problem solving, code correctness, and the ability to produce working solutions under single-attempt constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Attention (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: FACTS Benchmark Suite systematically evaluates factuality by testing whether model outputs remain grounded, accurate, and resistant to common hallucination modes across diverse factuality tasks. It is designed to probe truthfulness under realistic prompting rather than only simple trivia recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Attention (minor), Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Self-reflection, Inhibitory Control

Description: SimpleQA Verified is a short-form factual QA benchmark with verified answers, typically used to assess precision on straightforward information-seeking questions. It focuses on correctness and calibration in single-turn responses rather than long multi-step reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: Global PIQA evaluates practical physical commonsense reasoning across languages and cultures, often via questions about everyday interactions with objects and environments. It emphasizes selecting plausible actions or outcomes grounded in implicit physics and affordances rather than specialized technical knowledge.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3:

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) is a long-context evaluation where multiple similar “needle” requests are embedded in long multi-round conversational “haystacks,” and the model must retrieve and reproduce the correct referenced content. It stresses robust coreference tracking and resistance to distractors across long contexts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Working Memory, Attention
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates economically valuable, well-specified professional tasks across many occupations by judging the quality of produced work artifacts (e.g., slides, spreadsheets, schedules) against expert baselines. It is intended to measure end-to-end knowledge-work performance, not just question answering.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates agentic software engineering on realistic repository tasks that go beyond isolated bug fixes, emphasizing end-to-end patch delivery under constraints and potentially broader task formats. It is used to characterize real-world coding competence and robustness in applied development workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: Graphwalks tests long-context structured reasoning by embedding graph descriptions and requiring models to perform multi-step traversal tasks (e.g., BFS-like procedures or parent tracking) from text. It probes whether a model can maintain and manipulate a consistent internal representation of a combinatorial structure across many tokens.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Spatial Representation & Mapping, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: Toolathon evaluates how reliably models can use multiple tools (APIs, retrieval, code execution, or other utilities) to solve tasks that require correct call sequencing and integration of results. It emphasizes robustness to tool errors, correct parameterization, and coherent multi-step execution rather than purely linguistic answers.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: HMMT (Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament) benchmark sets consist of high-difficulty contest math problems that often require creative multi-step derivations and careful case analysis. As an evaluation set, it measures advanced mathematical reasoning and solution precision under no-tools or limited-tools settings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: FrontierMath is a benchmark of expert-level mathematics designed to be highly challenging at the frontier, with tiered difficulty and an emphasis on problems that resist shallow heuristics. It evaluates deep multi-step reasoning, formal manipulation, and, in tool-enabled settings, correct use of computation to support proofs or derivations.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Attention (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)
